meta.title: PCB — Your Local AI Workspace
meta.desc: PCB is a local AI workspace built on Oh My Pi. Finish work in plain language, or open the VS Code or Cursor already on your machine and use OMP-ckpt to review and restore AI edits. Open source, MIT.
hero.title: From a sentence in plain language to a product you can actually ship.
hero.lead: PCB is a local AI workspace built on Oh My Pi (OMP) and extended well beyond a chat window.
hero.lead2: We redesigned how you work with the AI. People who don't write code can collaborate in plain language. People who do can open the VS Code or Cursor already on their machine and develop with OMP and OMP-ckpt. From an idea, through a plan, to file changes and a product, the AI stays in the work.
hero.one: One package, two ways to use it. Use it directly, or extend it further if you develop.
hero.meta: Open source · MIT License · Windows · Local First
hero.visual.caption: The PCB workspace: project, conversation, plan and file changes in one place
hero.alt: The PCB workspace: projects and conversation on the left, the plan in the middle, files and results on the right
work.title: A place where work starts, not another chat box
work.lead: PCB is built on Oh My Pi (OMP). We did not write a second AI agent, and we did not add another conversation engine beside OMP. Every session is an OMP RPC subprocess running on this machine.
work.lead2: What we changed is the way you work with OMP, and the workflow around AI-assisted development.
ui.title: A calmer way to talk to the AI
ui.sub: People who don't program can still get real work done.
ui.body: We gave OMP a clearer graphical interface, and turned a developer-shaped interaction into steps that are easier to follow.
ui.chat.d: Talk in plain language, state what you need, and work through the question. This step does not change files.
ui.plan.d: The AI reads the project, analyses the request, and writes a plan you can inspect.
ui.build.d: After you approve the plan, OMP edits files and carries out the related tasks.
ui.review.d: Look at what actually changed, then accept it or restore an earlier state.
ui.note: You don't have to learn the underlying commands first. Conversation and a plan are enough to move the work forward.
dev.title: VS Code / Cursor + OMP + OMP-ckpt
dev.sub: A fuller environment for AI-assisted development.
dev.body: If you already work in code, PCB can be the front door to the project, not only a chat window. Open the desktop VS Code or Cursor already installed on this machine, and keep developing with OMP and OMP-ckpt.
ckpt.title: OMP-ckpt makes AI edits easier to inspect and easier to undo.
ckpt.body: It is there for the moment when the AI has changed many files and it is no longer obvious what moved, or how to go back.
ckpt.record.d: Checkpoints keep the state before and after the change.
ckpt.diff.d: See which files changed, and how.
ckpt.restore.d: When something is wrong, restore an earlier file state from a checkpoint.
ckpt.guard.d: The AI can take on harder edits, while you keep a place to review and roll back.
dev.note: Use PCB on its own, or step into the IDE and continue in the tools you already know.
make.title: From a development tool toward making a product
make.sub: Help with the code, and later with turning an idea into something people can see.
make.body: We want PCB to grow a longer path: build the software with AI, then use dedicated skills for a demo, the story around it, distribution and, eventually, selling it. That direction is spelled out in the roadmap below. None of it is available yet.
who.title: One package, for more than one kind of user
who.lead: PCB ships as one package. There is no everyday edition and no separate developer edition.
who.note: Opening an IDE is a habit, not a second product.
who.note2: If you don't write code, stay in PCB and work in language. If you do, open VS Code or Cursor whenever you want to inspect, edit and continue.
path.title: From Ideas to Products.
path.lead: Five steps. The first two are what you can do now. The last three are the roadmap.
path.s1.d: Describe the idea in plain language. The AI helps you plan it.
path.s2.d: OMP, your IDE and OMP-ckpt help you build it.
path.s3.d: A skill helps you make a product demo.
path.s4.d: Publish the product to social and promotion channels.
path.s5.d: Payment interfaces, for when a product is ready to sell.
path.note: What is true today is the PCB interface, the OMP integration and OMP-ckpt. Demos, publishing and payments are not described as features you can use now.
road.title: What we want PCB to be able to do next
road.lead: The next stage is more than a finished interface. It is the path from building a product to putting it in front of people. The three items below are planned. They are not available yet.
road.demo.d: Turn the way real products get built with PCB and OMP into a skill the AI can follow: shaping the idea, organising the build, showing the features and making a demo video.
road.social.t: Showing the product, and sharing it
road.social.d: Connect the demo to the channels where people actually see it. After the product exists, a skill can help prepare the introduction and the video, then publish them to supported social and promotion platforms.
road.pay.t: Payments, and a way to sell
road.pay.d: Infrastructure for a later commercial step: payment, purchase and related service interfaces, so software, digital goods and AI products can be sold.
sec.title: It runs locally. You keep the decisions.
sec.lead: PCB owns the interface, the workflow and the checks. OMP does the AI work.
sec.engine.d: OMP runs as a subprocess on this machine. It handles conversation, planning and file operations.
sec.local.d: The PCB service listens only on 127.0.0.1. This workspace is not exposed on the public network.
sec.auth.d: A plan runs only after you approve it. Dangerous commands ask again.
sec.file.d: Checkpoints and change review limit the risk of letting the AI edit a project.
sec.ide.d: Use the VS Code or Cursor already installed on this machine. PCB does not bundle an editor and does not download one.

faq.title: Questions
faq.lead: What it is, how OMP fits, and what is not available yet.
faq.a1: PCB is a local AI workspace built on Oh My Pi. It keeps plain language, the project, the plan and the file changes in one environment on your machine.
faq.q2: How does PCB relate to Oh My Pi?
faq.a2: Oh My Pi (OMP) is the AI engine on this machine. PCB does not ship a second agent. Each session is an OMP subprocess. PCB owns the interface, the workflow and the confirmation before anything changes.
faq.a3: It keeps checkpoints around AI file edits, so you can read the diff and restore an earlier state. This is available now. It is how continuous edits stay reversible.
faq.q4: Do I have to install VS Code or Cursor?
faq.a4: No. You can stay in PCB and never open an editor. When you want to inspect or keep editing code, open the desktop VS Code or Cursor already on this machine. PCB does not download an editor.
faq.q5: Will the AI change my files on its own?
faq.a5: Ordinary conversation does not change files. Work starts only after you approve a plan, and running a command asks again.
faq.q6: What if a change goes wrong?
faq.a6: You can inspect, accept or restore each change. The editor has the same keep and revert actions. For important projects, keep using Git as well.
faq.q7: Does this website upload my project?
faq.a7: No. This site only introduces PCB and offers the download. File operations happen on your computer. Whether a model request includes project content depends on the task and the model provider you choose.
faq.q8: Can I demo, publish or take payment today?
faq.a8: No. The demo skill, social publishing and payment interfaces are planned, and the page says so. Nothing here publishes for you or charges anyone yet.
bugs.title: Report a problem
bugs.lead: Open an issue on GitHub: say which build, which system, what you did and what you saw. Please do not paste API keys or source code.
about.title: About PCB
about.p1: PCB is an open-source project. We want it to be a local front door for people who don't write code and for people who do.
about.p2: It is more than a shell around OMP: the interface makes OMP usable by more people, and OMP-ckpt plus your IDE keep AI edits reviewable. Demos, publishing and payments stay on the roadmap.
